quote: The progress you make is always little by little... if you just walk through fog you will be wet, little by little, even though you don't know.
meaning: In 1965 Suzuki said practice is like walking in fog. You never feel it, but step by step you get soaked.

quote: One stumbles around bumping into the furniture, and gradually, you learn where each piece of furniture is, and finally... you find the light switch. You turn it on, and suddenly, it's all illuminated.
meaning: Bump around long enough and you learn the room, then the light comes on. Wiles worked seven years on Fermat's Last Theorem.

who: Zhu Xi · Commentary on the Great Learning, 1189
quote: After exerting himself in this way for a long time, he will suddenly find himself possessed of a wide and far-reaching penetration.
meaning: Keep studying and practising for a long time, and one day all the pieces suddenly connect.

who: Maryam Mirzakhani · Clay Mathematics Institute interview, 2008
quote: I did poorly in math for a couple of years in middle school... The beauty of mathematics only shows itself to more patient followers.
meaning: She struggled with math at school, but beauty appears to those who stay patient. In 2014 she won the Fields Medal.

quote: Great works are performed, not by strength, but perseverance... He that shall walk with vigour three hours a day will pass in seven years a space equal to the circumference of the globe.
meaning: Walking three hours a day for seven years equals a trip around the Earth. Steady daily work builds great things.

who: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky · Letter to Nadezhda von Meck, 1878
quote: ...I was working every day without any real inspiration... But my patience and faith did not fail me, and to-day I felt that inexplicable glow of inspiration...
meaning: Tchaikovsky composed every day even without feeling inspired. His patience paid off and the spark came. He wrote this in 1878.

who: Aesop · The Crow and the Pitcher, 1894
quote: Then he took another pebble and dropped it into the Pitcher... At last, at last, he saw the water mount up near him... Little by little does the trick.
meaning: One pebble seems useless, but pebble after pebble lifts the water. Many small efforts add up to success.

who: Ichiro Suzuki · Hall of Fame induction speech, 2025
quote: If you consistently do the little things, there's no limit [to] what you can achieve.
meaning: Small daily care adds up. Ichiro did this for 19 MLB seasons and joined the Hall of Fame in 2025.

who: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow · The Ladder of St. Augustine, 1858
quote: We have not wings, we cannot soar; / But we have feet to scale and climb / By slow degrees, by more and more, / The cloudy summits of our time.
meaning: We cannot fly to the top. We climb slowly, step by step, and that is how we get there.

quote: They were poor things to work with, but we managed it with patience, and little by little there arose solid walls of stone with moss and earth between.
meaning: With poor tools and patience, stone by stone, a hut slowly rose. Nansen and his partner built it in the Arctic in 1895.
